node.title: Customers
node.explanation: People who walk in. More of them means more cups sold.

node.title: Long queue
node.explanation: At busy times the line gets long, and some people leave without buying.

node.title: Cups sold
node.subtitle: Per day

node.explanation: How many drinks the shop sells in a day. Each cup brings in its price and uses up beans and milk.

node.title: Price per cup
node.explanation: What one drink costs the customer.
Cups sold multiplied by the price per cup.

node.title: Revenue
node.explanation: All the money that comes in from sales: cups sold times price per cup.

node.title: Costs
node.subtitle: Beans, milk, rent, staff
node.explanation: What the shop pays out. Beans and milk rise with every cup sold; rent and staff are paid however many cups the shop sells.

node.title: Profit
node.explanation: What is left of revenue after all costs are paid. This is the number the shop is run for.

edge.label: buy
edge.explanation: Customers buy drinks; each purchase is a cup sold.

edge.label: turns some away
edge.explanation: A long queue stops some sales: people who will not wait leave without a cup.
The number of cups sold feeds the multiplication.
The price per cup feeds the multiplication.
Cups sold times price per cup is the revenue.
More revenue means more profit, if costs stay the same.
Every cost paid comes out of revenue, so higher costs mean less profit.
